source: 1968 Chevrolet Chassis Service Manual, Rear Suspension and Drive Line, p.4-22

procedures.title: Rear torque control arm: remove, repair and install
steps: (continued) Disconnect the brake line at the caliper and from the torque arm; disconnect the parking brake cable.
Remove the pivot bolt and toe-in shims and pull the arm out of the frame. Tape the shims together and label them for reassembly.
Repairs: drill out the flared end of the bushing retainer with an 11/16" drill (see figure 57 in the manual).
Remove the special retainer plate and tap the retainer out of the bushing.
Spread the bushings apart with a chisel and tap them out of the arm (see figure 58 in the manual).
Lightly oil the outer diameters (not the rubber) of the new bushings and start them square in the arm.
Press the bushings in with J-7055-1 (see figure 59 in the manual).
With the bushings fully in, put the special plate over the flared part of a new retainer and push the retainer into the bushing.
Make a back-up plate for the flaring tool from 5/8" thick, 1-1/2" wide steel plate to the dimensions in figure 60 in the manual (about 5" long), drilled with clearance holes for two 1/2" bolts.

Set the back-up plate on the flared end of the retainer and bolt J-8111-23 to it with two 1/2" x 5" bolts, with the threaded hole of J-8111-23 centered over the unflared end and the chamfered retainer plate centered on the retainer tube.
Lightly oil the pointed end of screw J-8880-5 and thread it into J-8111-23 until it touches the retainer; keep threading until the retainer is flared (see figure 61 in the manual).
Installation: put the torque arm into the frame opening.
Put the toe-in shims back in their original places on both sides of the arm; fit the pivot bolt and tighten without final torque.
Lift the axle drive shaft into place and bolt it to the drive flange; torque the bolts to specification.
Lift the strut rod into place and insert the strut rod shaft...
notes: The arm may need to be forced outboard to give room to drop the drive shaft.
If the bushings are badly rusted in and the arm starts to spread during removal, hold it with a C-clamp.
For spindle support work, see Wheel Spindle and Support earlier in this section.
